task.description: Root-cause diagnosis of ISS-0524's claimed regression: mix letflow.check.test's wasm_hang discovery stage allegedly finding zero tagged tests after ISS-0418's fix.

result.note: NOT REPRODUCIBLE. All 5 real @tag :wasm_hang sites confirmed intact (plugin_handler_test.exs:153,390,493; call_timeout_test.exs:77; host_api_write_test.exs:459) -- ISS-0418 did not remove or retag anything, contrary to the issue's own stated premise. Live mix test --only wasm_hang --dry-run correctly discovers all 5. Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest passes consistently (6 passed, 5 repeated runs with distinct seeds, all green) -- its fixture (install_wasm_hang_aware_fake_mix/1) uses a fake mix binary independent of real repo tags, so it was never actually coupled to real wasm_hang tag count in the first place; the issue's theory doesn't even apply to this test. discover_wasm_hang_tests/0's parsing logic (bounded-window filter, already live-verified during ISS-0418) shows no bug against current real output shape. Root cause is most likely (d) a transient/environmental flake at TEST-RUNNER's original observation time (e.g. a resource-constrained host truncating the discovery subprocess's compile step before dry-run output was produced) -- the check's own hard-fail-on-empty-block behavior would correctly catch a genuinely-broken discovery run, which is working as designed, not evidence of a code defect. No surviving evidence of the original failure's raw output exists in handoffs/WF03-ISS0523-20260907/ to confirm this mechanism definitively. RECOMMENDATION: do not change discover_wasm_hang_tests/0's parsing logic or the test fixture (both currently correct, changing either would be unmotivated). Instead: (1) improve failure diagnosability by including the raw captured discovery output (or last N lines) in the existing Mix.raise message at lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex:434-441, so a future recurrence is diagnosable without a live repro; (2) optionally add a bounded single retry on an empty discovery block to rule out one-shot compile-race flakiness, WITHOUT changing the zero-tolerance policy itself (the moduledoc's own 'never silently proceed with zero' discipline should stay intact); (3) treat ISS-0524 as unconfirmed/likely transient in its own record unless it recurs.
